abstractions: Three operation IDs, four visits and four draft revisions. Recipients, text and SIM are one draft whose every change is an edit.
One native call is in flight at a time: a second send while the native review is open is refused as busy without a journal record and is not modeled.

The journal is reduced to one status per ID. Sent and delivery evidence, and startup reconciliation of an interrupted dispatch, are nondeterministic status advances; part counts and provider rows are covered by the journal tests.
The messaging-app handoff, which sends nothing itself, and the retired-ID watermark are outside the model.
Six read epochs and four visits. A read is one answer: status, send history and one page are not interleaved separately, since each stage applies the same epoch and active check.
Rows, threads and receipts are one content flag; the page cursor is one flag.
SMS read access is a native fact that changes outside any read. The session learns it only from a status answer.
Six read epochs and four page sizes (50 to 200 rows). The status read and the list read are one answer under one epoch check.
Availability changes and the adapter synchronisation that follows them are one step: the adapter synchronises on every component update and visibility change.
Search text and the selected contact are not modeled; a search is a read that resets the page size.
Four host attempts, three holds and three automatic sends. The host is reduced to its installed attempt and its send cooldown; IdentitySession models the host in full.
Each step is a start and one outcome. Cancelling a step in flight, the passkey refusal after an email code, and the required-sign-in page that cannot be closed are not modeled.
The readiness answer is ready or unavailable; which optional methods it offers is not modeled.
The host losing its in-memory attempt is an explicit event, so the agreement between the code step and the host is checked for every other step.
Six checks and three counted failures; the backoff delay itself is a nondeterministic timer.
The entitlement lifetime is two classes, live and lapsed, moved by a clock event. The refresh hint and the retry bound to the expiry are one armed timer.
A check is one answer: a signed active or ended plan, a billing snapshot, credits, a verified absence, an unpublished source, a transient failure, or an account refusal.
Two sign-ins and four record writes. The record age is fresh or old against the seven-day window; a plan end is none, ahead or past.
Cloud's answers are classes: no usable account, unreachable, billing unavailable, an admitting plan with or without a reported period end, credits, and a verified absence of a plan.
Applying the binding to the agent (bind, unbind, unconfirmed removal) is ConnectionController and ResidentRuntime scope; here the admission's requested binding is the binding.
Three attempts and two Cloud sessions (plus signed out). State tokens are match or no match.
An aborted wait has no further effect in the code, so cancel and retirement end the run in one step.
The session change and the flow's subscription seeing it are separate steps, so the check made when the wait ends is exercised.
Granted capabilities and the account read are GoogleAccounts scope; here a refresh is a counter.
One account, two authorizations and two status checks. The retained return is one of the shapes CallbackLanding hands over (a code, an error, neither) or a return for another account.
Cloud's state for the authorization is an input that completion and time can change. A failed step leaves everything as it was except that the return has been read.
Revocation of granted access, the account switch that reloads the panel, and the secure-store compare-exchange conflicts are not modeled.
Two environments, six calls. An answer is fresh or stale against its time limit; what it offers is not modeled.
A measurement that throws is the not-ready answer, cached like any other. A failed write of the stored copy is not modeled.
A process restart drops memory and the calls waiting on a probe; storage stays.
Four automatic retries (the backoff table), four rebinds and one turn. A start or rebind is one step with one outcome; its internals are ResidentRuntime scope.
The steps that hold the slot are classes: start, rebind, a history edit or voice preparation, a native sign-in return, and any other.
The rebind backoff is a flag cleared by time. Dialog contents, messages and errors are not modeled.
The retry timer armed before a start that ends in a recovery review is not cancelled by the code and is modeled as it is.
Test-mocks emulator transport only. Two requests, four proposals and three context revisions.
An answer carries zero to two proposals that are all bound correctly or refused together; the operation validation is part of that binding.
The dispatched action reports any result; the proposal is consumed either way.
Contacts is the only view admitted at runtime; Home and Notes stand for every other view.
The image capability is a native fact the shell learns only on a refresh (start and each return to the app).
The development-server profile, which ignores image admission, is not modeled.
Six issued sequence numbers. Pause and Turn off are one action whose answer is the listener's state afterwards.
A status read reports the listener as it was when the read was issued.
The other capability reads, the abort of a superseded refresh and the Settings instance check are not modeled.
Two sign-ins and owners, four attempt IDs, five wrong-code attempts and three ack attempts.
Opaque PKCE states, proofs and credentials are represented by identities. Cryptography, endpoint shapes and encrypted persistence are checked by existing implementation tests.

begin with a code method is the send and Cloud's acceptance in one step, and exchanged is the session and an immediate Authorize in one step; beginSend/sendAccepted/sendFailed and sessionReady/authorize/decline/consentTimeout are the same paths step by step.

Storage failure before the key commit ends the attempt. After key persistence, cancellation cannot stop acknowledgement. Authentication delivery precedes best-effort Steward logout and local-session cleanup.
The renderer is reduced to the attempt its code or MFA step names; SignInChooser models the renderer.
The browser development bridge (scripts/browser-cloud-dev-bridge.ts) is a separate sign-in implementation outside this model: it acknowledges the key before storing it and keeps no receipt.

stateMapping.wrongCodes/mfa/cooldown/sendsAccepted: failedVerifies, the MFA challenge and the send cooldown started only by an accepted send
stateMapping.authorized: Android's consent prompt before the key request
stateMapping.receipt/key/acknowledged/ackTries: persisted ack receipt, credential slot and acknowledge rounds

abstractions: Opaque exact-route categories summarize URL/method/body validation: identity, maps, gmail, calendar, self-revoke, billing, entitlement, redeem, cli-session and google-account. The parser remains covered by runtime tests.
Server authorization is explicit input to dispatch, separate from cached UI entitlement.

Two expiry ticks apply only to signed entitlements. The view is not derived from the clock: a lifetime that ran out still reads active until a check completes, and a failed check then reports it expired.
A token that cannot be verified is a failed check, never a refusal. Failed snapshot or credit refresh produces an unavailable view; none of these unbinds inference.
The stored admission record is fresh or stale against its seven-day window and plan end. PlanAdmissionGrace models its plan end and writes in detail.
Whether the on-device agent itself is running is ResidentRuntime and ConnectionController scope and is not a variable here.

stateMapping.plan/validFor/refresh/failedSinceLapse: EntitlementRefresher cached signed entitlement, its lifetime and the lapse reported once a failed check completes
stateMapping.signedRefusal/credits: signed refusal versus authenticated organization-credit fallback
stateMapping.bound/admittedBy: the running agent's inference binding and whether Cloud's answer or the stored record admitted it
stateMapping.grace/graceOwner/graceEpoch: the stored plan admission record and the sign-in it was verified for
stateMapping.request/dispatched/refusedRequests: managedServiceRequest and private Google broker admission, including refused routes
stateMapping.source/fallback: signed entitlement, absent-token billing snapshot and signed-no-plan credit supplementation

abstractions: Two Google connections and two connect attempts represent arbitrary opaque IDs.
Partial Gmail write capabilities are grouped as modify for the reviewed-operation gate. Calendar read/write differences are further modeled by CalendarSync.
A return requests fresh account readback and does not itself grant capabilities. GoogleConnectRuntime models the wait itself.
An unconfirmed disconnect leaves the account as it was shown; the unknown account list is not a separate value.

stateMapping.attempt/pendingEpoch/phase/returnMatched: googleConnect waiting, matching state, foreground return and the bounded wait; refreshing is the account re-read the readers own
stateMapping.note/noteEpoch: the denied or failed status kept as a note until the next start or a Cloud session change
stateMapping.disconnectSent/disconnectResult/revoked: one disconnect request and its disconnected, still-connected or unconfirmed result

abstractions: Opaque credential contents and provider configurations are equality classes; providerRevision captures the full stored provider comparison.
Current versus retained byte caps are scaled to two and three units, with four representing preflight overflow.
The running resident is stopped only for matching bound critical changes. No-provider Cloud sign-in and ordinary slots may commit without stopping it.
Rollback restores only its captured provider revision. A newer provider revision makes it fail without overwriting it.
The Cloud-change observer is notified for the production Cloud slot by name. The staging slot exists only with test mocks and its writes do not reach the observer.

stateMapping.operation/phase/before/capturedProvider: mutateSlotOnce classification and slot/provider snapshot reread
stateMapping.requestedStop/acknowledgedStop/stopped: exact strict resident shutdown before critical write
stateMapping.ownerEpoch/capturedEpoch: credential intent and lifecycle ownership recheck
stateMapping.oldSize/newSize/admissionInvalidated: retained slot-cap shrink versus rejected growth after admission invalidation
stateMapping.productionSlot/observerNotified: the Cloud-change observer, called for the provider slot and for a changed production Cloud credential only

abstractions: Finite representative operation and payload identities. See application README for source contract and evidence.
The prototype call screen shows mute, speaker and hold from the moment it opens, before the call is live. The keypad and assistant toggles are not modeled.
A decline with a quick reply leaves no voicemail. Every transition changes prototype state only; there is no variable for real effects because no transition has one.
Finite representative identities and contents. Exact source symbols and modeling limits are documented in the family README.
The device controls need test mocks, the development server, a non-Android page and ?tools=1. The runtime profile is a query choice that admits nothing.
Model safety checks do not establish implementation refinement or device acceptance.
One private profile, two credentials and requests, serial resident replacement. The deployment environment is fixed for the run and is not constrained by an invariant.
The runtime launchers are developer infrastructure with local/private process and storage boundaries.
The bridge's own email sign-in acknowledges the minted key before storing it and keeps no receipt; that order is outside this model, which starts from a received claim.
